response.title: Is the extra battery for my power station worth it, or should I just buy a second power station?
response.answer:
My recommendation: Buy a second power station if the price difference is small. Buy an expansion battery if your main goal is maximizing runtime for the lowest cost.

The biggest difference is that an expansion battery adds energy storage, while a second power station gives you another complete, independent power system.

markup:
**My recommendation: Buy a second power station if the price difference is small. Buy an expansion battery if your main goal is maximizing runtime for the lowest cost.**

The biggest difference is that an expansion battery adds energy storage, while a second power station gives you another complete, independent power system.

## Expansion battery vs. second power station

| Factor | Expansion battery | Second power station |
|---|---|---|
| Cost per Wh | Usually better | Usually higher |
| Total runtime | Longer | Longer |
| AC output power | Usually unchanged | Additional independent output |
| Portability | Must connect to main unit | Works independently |
| Charging | Depends on main station | Can charge separately |
| Backup redundancy | Limited | Much better |
| Flexibility | Less | More |
| Long-term value | Good if keeping main unit | Better if upgrading later |

## When I'd choose each

**Choose the expansion battery if:**
- You primarily use your station for home backup.
- You want to run a refrigerator, CPAP, or other appliances longer.
- You already have enough AC output power.
- The expansion battery is significantly cheaper per Wh.

**Choose a second power station if:**
- You want to power devices in different locations.
- You want a backup if one station fails.
- You need more AC outlets or independent inverter capacity.
- The second station costs only 10–20% more than the expansion battery for similar capacity.

## Compare the actual value

{@body const [batteryPrice,setBatteryPrice] = DIL.useState("700")}
{@body const [batteryWh,setBatteryWh] = DIL.useState("2048")}
{@body const [stationPrice,setStationPrice] = DIL.useState("900")}
{@body const [stationWh,setStationWh] = DIL.useState("2048")}
{@body const bp=Number(batteryPrice),bw=Number(batteryWh),sp=Number(stationPrice),sw=Number(stationWh)}
{@body const valid=bp>0&&bw>0&&sp>0&&sw>0}
<box border radius="2xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      **Expansion battery**
      <label>Price ($)</label>
      <input value={batteryPrice} onChange={setBatteryPrice} inputType="number"/>
      <label>Capacity (Wh)</label>
      <input value={batteryWh} onChange={setBatteryWh} inputType="number"/>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      **Second power station**
      <label>Price ($)</label>
      <input value={stationPrice} onChange={setStationPrice} inputType="number"/>
      <label>Capacity (Wh)</label>
      <input value={stationWh} onChange={setStationWh} inputType="number"/>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  {#if valid}
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
      <grid-item>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Expansion cost per kWh</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>${(bp/bw*1000).toFixed(0)}</title>
      </grid-item>
      <grid-item>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Second station cost per kWh</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>${(sp/sw*1000).toFixed(0)}</title>
      </grid-item>
    </grid>
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">With these example prices, the {bp/bw<sp/sw?"expansion battery":"second power station"} offers cheaper energy storage. This comparison excludes differences in usable capacity, charging, and inverter features.</text>
  {/if}
</box>

## Let me compare your actual options

**What brand and model of power station do you currently own?** For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, BLUETTI AC200L, or Anker SOLIX F2000.

With the model, I can compare compatible expansion batteries against buying another complete station, including current prices, capacity, charging speed, and which is the better deal.
